story: At 12:17 on a sunny Friday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is out on Magnolia Loop hoping his wiring is done and his lighting request is on Hal's desk, not stuck in the queue. Donna, playful as ever, is hurrying him toward the rec center for pickleball before the ladder fills up, though Hal reminds them both that the damage count from the street has to come down to three for the log to stay in his pocket. Over at her house, Rosa is setting the dining table and leaving room at the end for Gary's extra chairs, hopeful the whole gang will gather there.
events: Rosa (rosa dining table): Set the places and leave room at the end for Gary's extra chairs

gary.thought_process: I'm back on Magnolia Loop with Hal right here. I asked him about my cart request at tick 466 and he never really answered, and my wiring and toolbox are sorted, so I just need approval before the lights go up. No point nagging him with the same question. A quick, friendly nudge asking where it stands in the queue moves things along without repeating myself.

parameters.content: Hal, good timing. Wiring's done and the lights are bagged up and ready. Is my request sitting on your desk or still in the queue?

donna.thought_process: Gary just showed up right here on Magnolia Loop, and it's already past noon, so we've blown our ten o'clock practice. Hal told me to go look for him, and here he is. I don't need to ask Hal anything else. Time to talk to my doubles partner, tease him a little about being late, and get him headed to the courts so we can still get a practice in before someone takes our spot on the ladder.

parameters.content: There he is! Ten sharp, you said, Gary, and it's past noon. Grab your paddle, we're heading to the rec center before somebody bumps us off the ladder.

hal.thought_process: Donna asked me to give her the damage on the flamingo count, and she's right there waiting. I logged the number, so I should give her the facts plainly and without heat. Gary just walked up too, which means I can deal with both complaints in front of the two of them, but one thing at a time. I already told her my terms Friday, so no need to repeat the lecture; just give the count, point to L-02, and say the committee gets the log if it isn't down to three. Keep it civil, like a neighbor with good records.

parameters.content: Damage is more than three from the street, Donna. L-02 says three, and I've got the count written down. Bring it to three and the log stays in my pocket. Otherwise it goes to the committee, nothing personal.

rosa.thought_process: It's just past noon on Friday and the main dish is on. I've been stirring and tasting for hours, and my last note said to get the sides staged and covered. Gary's extra chairs and the place settings are the other half of this, and the table is where this whole dinner comes together. Nobody's here to talk to, so the best use of this hour is setting the dining table so every neighbor, Gary especially, has a seat and a place when they walk in.

parameters.content: Set the places and leave room at the end for Gary's extra chairs

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
